title: Knowledge check: CORS and Cross-Origin API Access

questions.prompt: In CORS and Cross-Origin API Access, which statement best describes Origin and browser security model?
options: Configure the origins, methods and headers required by the application rather than using an unrestricted allowlist. CORS controls browser access; it does not authenticate requests or authorize data changes.
This option describes a different concept and does not define origin and browser security model (choice 2).
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Configure the origins, methods and headers required by the application rather than using an unrestricted allowlist. CORS controls browser access; it does not authenticate requests or authorize data changes.
questions.explanation: Configure the origins, methods and headers required by the application rather than using an unrestricted allowlist. CORS controls browser access; it does not authenticate requests or authorize data changes.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying CORS and Cross-Origin API Access?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.
questions.answer_key: Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.
questions.explanation: Model API paths around resources and align method/status-code semantics with the operation. Use consistent response envelopes, versioning, CORS configuration, idempotency where appropriate, and API documentation.

questions.prompt: A change related to CORS and Cross-Origin API Access appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
